title: AV-FLARE: Feature-Level Reliability Estimation for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
abstract: arXiv:2611.28327v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition (MMER) systems typically rely on learned feature representations and attention mechanisms that implicitly weight information across time and modalities. However, these mechanisms do not explicitly incorporate input reliability, despite the presence of noise in audio, occlusions in visual data, and the sparse and event-driven nature of affective cues. We propose AV-FLARE, a framework that explicitly estimates fine-grained reliability scores across both temporal and feature dimensions prior to temporal modeling and uses them to modulate feature representations. Reliability is computed using two complementary components: (i) a supervised network trained jointly with the classification objective, and (ii) an unsupervised Gaussian Mixture Model that models global feature distributions. translated_abstract: 多模态情感识别（MMER）系统通常依赖于学习得到的特征表示和注意力机制，这些机制在时间和模态维度上隐式地对信息进行加权。然而，这些机制并未显式地纳入输入可靠性，尽管音频中存在噪声、视觉数据中存在遮挡，且情感线索具有稀疏性和事件驱动的特性。我们提出了AV-FLARE，该框架在时间建模之前显式估计跨越时间和特征两个维度的细粒度可靠性评分，并利用这些评分来调节特征表示。可靠性通过两个互补的组件计算：（i）与分类目标联合训练的监督网络，以及（ii）对全局特征分布进行建模的无监督高斯混合模型。这些信号被结合起来，从而同时提供任务驱动和分布感知的可靠性估计。为了整合模态，我们（注：原摘要在此处不完整）
tldr: 提出AV-FLARE框架，通过监督网络与无监督高斯混合模型相结合，在时间建模前显式估计时间和特征维度上的细粒度可靠性评分并以此调节特征表示，从而提升多模态情感识别对噪声与信息缺失的鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: AV-FLARE explicitly estimates fine-grained reliability scores across temporal and feature dimensions by combining a supervised network with an unsupervised Gaussian Mixture Model, and uses them to modulate feature representations for more robust multimodal emotion recognition.
